blocks.text: The gleaming chrome on a motorcycle in Aba was put there atom by atom, using electricity to force metal ions out of solution and onto the steel. That is electrolysis, and the same process purifies copper, extracts aluminium and makes the chlorine used to treat drinking water.

blocks.title: Electrolysis
blocks.text: Electrolysis is the decomposition of a compound by the passage of an electric current through it in the molten state or in aqueous solution. An electrolyte is a substance that conducts electricity in the molten or aqueous state and is chemically decomposed in the process.

rows: NaCl solution, dilute H2SO4, NaOH solution
Ethanoic acid, aqueous ammonia, carbonic acid
Sugar solution, ethanol, kerosene, pure water
blocks.caption: Electrolytes conduct by moving ions; metals conduct by moving electrons and are not decomposed

blocks.markdown:
## What happens at each electrode

- The **cathode** is the electrode connected to the negative terminal. Positive ions, **cations**, migrate to it, gain electrons and are **reduced**.
- The **anode** is the electrode connected to the positive terminal. Negative ions, **anions**, migrate to it, lose electrons and are **oxidised**.

A reliable memory aid: **RedCat** and **AnOx** — reduction at the cathode, oxidation at the anode.

For molten sodium chloride with inert electrodes:

- Cathode: Na+ + e- -> Na (silvery molten sodium)
- Anode: 2Cl- -> Cl2 + 2e- (pale green gas)

## Preferential discharge in aqueous solution

Water itself supplies H+ and OH- ions, so an aqueous electrolyte always offers a choice at each electrode. Three factors decide which ion is discharged.

1. **Position in the electrochemical series** — the ion lower in the discharge series is released more readily. At the cathode the order of ease of discharge is K+, Ca2+, Na+, Mg2+, Al3+, Zn2+, Fe2+, Pb2+, H+, Cu2+, Ag2+ with the easiest at the right-hand end. At the anode the order is SO4 2-, NO3-, Cl-, Br-, I-, OH-, again easiest at the right.
2. **Concentration** — a very concentrated ion may be discharged in preference to one that is normally favoured. Concentrated brine gives chlorine rather than oxygen for this reason.
3. **Nature of the electrode** — an active electrode such as copper dissolves at the anode instead of releasing a gas.

blocks.title: Electrolysis of dilute sodium chloride solution with inert electrodes
blocks.prompt: Predict the products at each electrode when dilute sodium chloride solution is electrolysed using platinum electrodes, and write the half equations.

steps.text: List the ions present. From the salt: Na+ and Cl-. From the water: H+ and OH-.
At the cathode the competition is between Na+ and H+. Hydrogen lies below sodium in the discharge series, so H+ is discharged preferentially.
Cathode half equation: 2H+ + 2e- -> H2. Hydrogen gas is given off, which pops with a lighted splint.
At the anode the competition is between Cl- and OH-. The hydroxide ion is discharged more readily, and because the solution is dilute the chloride concentration is too low to override this.
Anode half equation: 4OH- -> 2H2O + O2 + 4e-. Oxygen is given off, which relights a glowing splint.
The Na+ and Cl- ions remain in solution, so the liquid becomes a more concentrated sodium chloride solution. In effect the water has been electrolysed.
Note the contrast: if the brine were concentrated, chlorine would be produced at the anode instead, which is the basis of the industrial chlor-alkali process.

blocks.answer: Hydrogen at the cathode and oxygen at the anode; the solution becomes more concentrated sodium chloride

rows: Molten Al2O3 in cryolite, carbon electrodes
Oxygen, which burns the carbon anode away

blocks.title: Purifying copper
blocks.text: In electrolytic refining the impure copper is the anode and a thin sheet of pure copper is the cathode, with copper(II) sulphate solution as the electrolyte. Copper dissolves from the anode as Cu2+ and plates onto the cathode as pure metal. Impurities such as silver and gold fall below the anode as anode sludge.

blocks.title: List every ion before you decide
blocks.text: Begin every aqueous electrolysis answer by writing the four ions present, including H+ and OH- from water. Students who skip that step routinely forget that water is competing and give the wrong product.

points: An electrolyte conducts by the movement of ions and is decomposed; a metal conducts by electrons and is not.
Reduction happens at the cathode and oxidation at the anode.
In aqueous solution H+ and OH- from water compete with the ions of the solute.
Discharge depends on position in the electrochemical series, concentration and the nature of the electrode.
Concentrated brine yields chlorine at the anode, while dilute brine yields oxygen.
An active copper anode dissolves rather than releasing a gas, which is the basis of electrolytic refining.
